note: Metric catalog (layer 1). Generated by DeepSeek agents I1-I3 against METRIK-PARAMETER-VERTRAG.md, merged by Claude Code 19.11.2026. Weights are a first guess, tune freely.

metrics.name: Word count
metrics.compute: Strip punctuation, split on whitespace, count tokens.
metrics.rationale: Longer prompts carry more content (density), more production momentum (tempo) and more activation (energy).

metrics.name: Type-token ratio
metrics.compute: Unique lowercase word types divided by total tokens.
metrics.rationale: Varied vocabulary signals exploratory breadth (openness) and less repetitive, conceptually deeper text.

metrics.name: Measure of textual lexical diversity
metrics.compute: Forward and reverse MTLD with a 0.72 TTR threshold, mean of both factors.
metrics.rationale: Sustained lexical variety over a longer stretch indicates sustained focus on one exploration (attention) plus depth.

metrics.name: Mean word length
metrics.compute: Mean character count of alphabetic tokens.
metrics.rationale: Longer words pack more information per token and correlate with formal, abstract register.

metrics.name: Long-word ratio
metrics.compute: Share of tokens with 7 or more characters.
metrics.rationale: Latinate multi-syllable vocabulary is the classic marker of formal, abstract, information-dense prose.

metrics.name: Mean syllables per word
metrics.compute: Mean syllable count per token using a vowel-group heuristic.
metrics.rationale: Polysyllabic words slow delivery and mark a measured, formal, reflective tone.

metrics.name: Function-word ratio
metrics.compute: Closed-class words (articles, prepositions, auxiliaries, conjunctions, pronouns) divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: High function-word density reflects grammatically elaborated, formal, structurally dense sentences.

metrics.name: Noun ratio
metrics.compute: Nouns divided by tokens via POS tagging.
metrics.rationale: Nominal style is dense, formal and tends toward abstract entities rather than actions.

metrics.name: Verb ratio
metrics.compute: Verbs divided by tokens via POS tagging.
metrics.rationale: Verb-heavy, action-oriented language reads as faster and more energized than nominal style.

metrics.name: Adjective ratio
metrics.compute: Adjectives divided by tokens via POS tagging.
metrics.rationale: Descriptive qualification adds texture and evaluative warmth to otherwise bare statements.

metrics.name: Adverb ratio
metrics.compute: Adverbs (excluding not) divided by tokens via POS tagging.
metrics.rationale: Intensifying and manner adverbs add pace and liveliness to the phrasing.

metrics.name: Pronoun ratio
metrics.compute: All personal and possessive pronouns divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: Pronoun-dense text is interpersonal and informal rather than distanced and institutional.

metrics.name: First-person singular ratio
metrics.compute: Count of I, me, my, mine, myself divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: Self-reference is the strongest single marker of personal, close, informal talk.

metrics.name: Second-person ratio
metrics.compute: Count of you, your, yours, yourself divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: Direct address creates interpersonal warmth and keeps the exchange mutually focused.

metrics.name: First-person plural ratio
metrics.compute: Count of we, us, our, ours divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: We-language builds a shared frame, which reads as close, warm and jointly exploratory.

metrics.name: Modal verb ratio
metrics.compute: Count of can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will, would divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: Modal framing hedges commitment and opens alternatives, which lowers felt certainty.

metrics.name: Negation ratio
metrics.compute: Count of not, n't, never, no, none, nothing, neither, nor divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: Frequent negation correlates with defensive, cooler, less settled phrasing.

metrics.name: Emoji ratio
metrics.compute: Unicode emoji count per sentence via property escapes.
metrics.rationale: Emoji are a direct, reliable signal of playful, warm, informal register.

metrics.name: Hedge ratio
metrics.compute: Count of maybe, perhaps, possibly, probably, kind of, sort of, I think, seems, apparently per 10 tokens.
metrics.rationale: Explicit hedging is the most direct lexical cue of hesitation and reduced certainty.

metrics.name: Sentence count
metrics.compute: Count of sentences from sentence segmentation.
metrics.rationale: More sentences per prompt mean more points made quickly, i.e. denser and faster output.

metrics.name: Mean sentence length
metrics.compute: Tokens divided by sentence count.
metrics.rationale: Long sentences are information-dense and deliberate, which reads as slow rather than snappy.

metrics.name: Clause nesting depth
metrics.compute: Mean depth of subordinate clause nesting from the dependency parse.
metrics.rationale: Nested subordination is the clearest syntactic proxy for abstraction and sustained focus.

metrics.name: Subordinating-conjunction ratio
metrics.compute: Count of because, although, while, since, unless, whereas, if, that, which, who per sentence.
metrics.rationale: Explicit causal and concessive links mark reasoning-heavy, composed, formal prose.

metrics.name: Punctuation density
metrics.compute: Non-terminal punctuation marks divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: Heavy punctuation chopping accompanies fast, dense, less composed delivery.

metrics.name: Question ratio
metrics.compute: Sentences ending in a question mark divided by sentences.
metrics.rationale: Questions open the space and signal engagement, while conceding that the user does not yet know.

metrics.name: Exclamation ratio
metrics.compute: Sentences ending in an exclamation mark divided by sentences.
metrics.rationale: Exclamations are among the strongest surface cues of high activation and arousal.

metrics.name: Passive-voice ratio
metrics.compute: Passive clauses divided by total clauses via parse match.
metrics.rationale: Agentless passive constructions read as detached and formal, so they cool the exchange.

metrics.name: Future-tense ratio
metrics.compute: Future auxiliaries (will, shall, 'll) divided by verbs.
metrics.rationale: Future reference points away from the settled present, which reads as more open and less certain.

metrics.name: Conditional ratio
metrics.compute: Conditional constructions (if + would/could/should/might) per sentence.
metrics.rationale: Hypothetical framing expands possibility space and explicitly withholds commitment.

metrics.name: Contraction ratio
metrics.compute: Apostrophe contractions (don't, it's, I'm) divided by tokens.
metrics.rationale: Contractions are the most reliable orthographic marker of informal, fast, personal speech.

metrics.name: Flesch Reading Ease
metrics.compute: 206.835 - 1.015*(words/sentences) - 84.6*(syllables/words).
metrics.rationale: Easy, plain text is skimmed fast and stays surface-level and informal; dense text slows it down.

metrics.name: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level
metrics.compute: 0.39*(words/sentences) + 11.8*(syllables/words) - 15.59.
metrics.rationale: Higher grade level means more formal, more information-dense, more abstract wording.

metrics.name: Gunning Fog Index
metrics.compute: 0.4*((words/sentences) + 100*(polysyllables/words)).
metrics.rationale: Fog weights polysyllables explicitly, which tracks formal register and conceptual load.

metrics.name: SMOG Index
metrics.compute: 1.043*sqrt(30*(polysyllables/sentences)) + 3.1291.
metrics.rationale: SMOG is poly-syllable driven, so it rises with formal, dense, abstract phrasing.

metrics.name: Coleman-Liau Index
metrics.compute: 0.0588*L - 0.296*S - 15.8, with L letters per 100 words and S sentences per 100 words.
metrics.rationale: Character-based instead of syllable-based, giving an independent estimate of formal, slow-reading text.

metrics.name: Automated Readability Index
metrics.compute: 4.71*(chars/words) + 0.5*(words/sentences) - 21.43.
metrics.rationale: Letter-heavy, long-sentence text is exactly the formal, dense, abstract register the index measures.

metrics.name: Sentiment valence (AFINN/VADER lexicon sum)
metrics.compute: Tokenize prompt, sum AFINN scores of known words, divide by token count, average with VADER compound if available.
metrics.rationale: Positive valence reads as warm, easy and nearer; negative valence cools the surface.

metrics.name: Arousal / intensity (VADER cues)
metrics.compute: Count exclamation marks, ALL-CAPS words, intensifiers (very, so, really) and negation flips; combine into an intensity score per sentence.
metrics.rationale: Intensity is the textbook arousal signal: high activation, low calm, faster perceived pace.

metrics.name: Dominance (NRC-VAD idea)
metrics.compute: Mean dominance value over known tokens using a small hand-curated VAD seed list (control/agency words high, helplessness words low).
metrics.rationale: Dominant language signals control and assertiveness, feeding certainty and active energy.

metrics.name: Joy lexicon density
metrics.compute: Share of tokens in a joy seed list (happy, love, great, glad, excited, thanks-adjacent).
metrics.rationale: Joy vocabulary warms the tone, lightens it and adds activation.

metrics.name: Anger lexicon density
metrics.compute: Share of tokens in an anger seed list (angry, hate, awful, ridiculous, furious).
metrics.rationale: Anger raises tension and heat: calm down, warmth down, energy up.

metrics.name: Fear/anxiety lexicon density
metrics.compute: Share of tokens in a fear seed list (afraid, worried, scary, anxious, nervous).
metrics.rationale: Anxiety reads as unsettled and uncertain, narrowing exploration.

metrics.name: Sadness lexicon density
metrics.compute: Share of tokens in a sadness seed list (sad, lonely, tired, lost, sorry-for-self).
metrics.rationale: Sadness is low-arousal withdrawal: energy down, slight quiet, less outward warmth.

metrics.name: Surprise markers
metrics.compute: Count surprise cues (wow, whoa, really?!, unexpected, surprise, interrobang) per sentence.
metrics.rationale: Surprise opens attention and play, and adds a burst of energy.

metrics.name: Affect punctuation (caps, !, ...)
metrics.compute: Ratio of exclamation marks, ellipses and ALL-CAPS tokens to total characters/tokens.
metrics.rationale: Loud punctuation reads as fast, loud and less settled.

metrics.name: Self-disclosure (I + feeling/state)
metrics.compute: Density of first-person singular pronouns co-occurring with feeling/state words in the same sentence.
metrics.rationale: Talking about one's own state creates intimacy and relaxes formality.

metrics.name: Positive/negative balance
metrics.compute: (pos_count - neg_count) / (pos_count + neg_count + 1) over valence lexicon hits.
metrics.rationale: Relative positivity is a robust, length-insensitive warmth signal.

metrics.name: Politeness markers
metrics.compute: Count please, kindly, if you don't mind, would you, may I; normalize per sentence.
metrics.rationale: Politeness signals social distance handling and considerate warmth.

metrics.name: Gratitude markers
metrics.compute: Count thanks, thank you, appreciate, grateful.
metrics.rationale: Gratitude is a direct warmth and relational-closeness cue.

metrics.name: Apology markers
metrics.compute: Count sorry, apologies, my mistake, excuse me.
metrics.rationale: Apology softens and de-escalates while admitting uncertainty.

metrics.name: Hedges / uncertainty markers
metrics.compute: Density of maybe, perhaps, I think, sort of, kind of, possibly, might.
metrics.rationale: Hedges are the canonical low-certainty, exploratory marker.

metrics.name: Boosters / certainty markers
metrics.compute: Density of definitely, absolutely, clearly, always, must, of course.
metrics.rationale: Boosters assert commitment: high certainty and drive.

metrics.name: Imperative mood
metrics.compute: Share of sentences tagged imperative via POS pattern (base verb in sentence-initial position, no subject).
metrics.rationale: Commands are direct, activating and fast-reading.

metrics.name: Open (wh-) questions
metrics.compute: Count sentences ending in ? whose first wh-word is what/why/how/who/where/when.
metrics.rationale: Wh-questions invite wide exploration and deeper framing.

metrics.name: Closed (yes/no) questions
metrics.compute: Count ? sentences not starting with a wh-word (aux-initial or tag questions).
metrics.rationale: Yes/no questions narrow the field to a single point.

metrics.name: Request / directive markers
metrics.compute: Count can you, could you, would you, I need, help me, please + verb.
metrics.rationale: Requests presume a relationship and usually open a new line of inquiry.

metrics.name: Humor / irony markers
metrics.compute: Count haha, lol, :), jokes, exaggeration cues, scare quotes, 'sure...' irony patterns; combine.
metrics.rationale: Humor is the clearest playfulness signal and loosens formality.

metrics.name: Speech act class (directive share)
metrics.compute: Rule-based classification per sentence into assertive/directive/commissive/expressive; return share of directive+commissive.
metrics.rationale: Action-oriented acts read as committed and driving; explicit approximation.

metrics.name: Vocative / direct address
metrics.compute: Count second-person pronouns (you/your) plus greeting names (hey, hi) at sentence start.
metrics.rationale: Addressing someone directly builds nearness and informality.

metrics.name: Modal verb force
metrics.compute: Weighted count of modals: must/shall/will (+1), should/would (0.5), could/might/may (0.2), divided by clauses.
metrics.rationale: Strong modals formalize and commit; weak modals leave room to explore.

metrics.name: Concreteness (lexical)
metrics.compute: Mean concreteness over known nouns/verbs using a compact concreteness seed table (Brysbaert-style, ~500 words).
metrics.rationale: Concrete language is tangible, grounded and shallow-abstraction.

metrics.name: Abstractness (suffix + word class)
metrics.compute: Share of abstract-noun suffixes (-tion, -ness, -ity, -ism, -ment) plus abstract seed words.
metrics.rationale: Abstract nouns signal conceptual depth and formal register.

metrics.name: Topic keyword density
metrics.compute: Top non-stopword content-word frequency divided by content tokens.
metrics.rationale: Repeating a few content words shows the user is holding one topic.

metrics.name: Topic coherence (sentence overlap)
metrics.compute: Mean Jaccard overlap of content-word sets between consecutive sentences.
metrics.rationale: Lexical chaining across sentences is a direct focus/coherence proxy.

metrics.name: Past time reference
metrics.compute: Density of past-tense verbs plus yesterday, ago, last, used to, was/were.
metrics.rationale: Looking back is reflective, settled and slower than forward drive.

metrics.name: Future time reference
metrics.compute: Density of will, going to, tomorrow, next, plan, soon, shall.
metrics.rationale: Future talk opens possibility space and adds forward drive, while plans are still unsettled.

metrics.name: Pronoun focus (you vs I)
metrics.compute: (you_count - i_count) / (you_count + i_count + 1).
metrics.rationale: Other-focus reads as outward attention and relational engagement.

metrics.name: Lexical diversity (type-token ratio)
metrics.compute: Unique content-word types divided by content tokens (length-normalized by root TTR).
metrics.rationale: Varied vocabulary implies information density and reflective elaboration.

metrics.name: Mean sentence length
metrics.compute: Mean tokens per sentence.
metrics.rationale: Long sentences carry more information, feel slower and more elaborate.

metrics.name: Readability (Flesch ease, inverted)
metrics.compute: Flesch Reading Ease = 206.835 - 1.015*(words/sentences) - 84.6*(syllables/words); invert.
metrics.rationale: Harder text correlates with formal, abstract, slow register.

metrics.name: Formality (Heylighen F-score)
metrics.compute: Heylighen F = (noun+adj+prep+article freq - pronoun+verb+adverb+interjection freq + 100) / 2.
metrics.rationale: Established formal-register measure; formal text is also less intimate and cooler.

metrics.name: Technical jargon / acronym density
metrics.compute: Share of unknown-but-multi-letter acronyms (e.g. API, LLM) plus a small technical-terms seed list.
metrics.rationale: Domain shorthand signals expertise, depth and packed information.

metrics.name: Curiosity / exploration words
metrics.compute: Count what if, wonder, explore, imagine, curious, idea, experiment, try.
metrics.rationale: Exploratory wording is the most direct semantic openness cue.

metrics.name: Typing speed (chars per second)
metrics.compute: Count printable keydown characters per composer session divided by active typing time (first to last keystroke, pauses over 5 s excluded).
metrics.rationale: Fast sustained typing reads as a quick, activated exchange.

metrics.name: Typing burst length
metrics.compute: Split a prompt into bursts at inter-key gaps over 1.5 s, take the median characters per burst.
metrics.rationale: Long unbroken bursts signal momentum and packed input.

metrics.name: Long-pause ratio while typing
metrics.compute: Share of inter-key intervals within a prompt that exceed 2 s.
metrics.rationale: Pausing mid-sentence indicates deliberation rather than reflex.

metrics.name: Median inter-key interval
metrics.compute: Median milliseconds between keystrokes inside bursts.
metrics.rationale: Slow keying is careful but also hesitant.

metrics.name: Backspace / correction ratio
metrics.compute: Backspace and Delete keydowns divided by all keydowns in the composer.
metrics.rationale: Heavy deletion means second-guessing the wording.

metrics.name: Hold before send
metrics.compute: Milliseconds from the last keystroke to the submit event.
metrics.rationale: Lingering before sending means weighing the message.

metrics.name: Latency to first keystroke after answer end
metrics.compute: Milliseconds from RESPONSE_END (or page mount) to the first keydown in the composer.
metrics.rationale: Long dead time suggests drift, yet a slow start can also be reflection.

metrics.name: Total think time per turn
metrics.compute: Time from first focus or keydown in the composer to SUBMIT, including pauses.
metrics.rationale: A long composed turn reads as deeper, slower processing.

metrics.name: Interruption rate (send during answer)
metrics.compute: Share of SUBMIT events dispatched while the store phase is thinking or speaking.
metrics.rationale: Barging in is high drive with low patience.

metrics.name: Prompt length (chars)
metrics.compute: Median character count of the last 10 submitted prompts.
metrics.rationale: Longer messages carry more information per turn.

metrics.name: Prompt length trend
metrics.compute: Ordinary least squares slope of prompt length over turn index, divided by mean length.
metrics.rationale: Growing prompts mean expanding scope and rising involvement.

metrics.name: Median turn interval
metrics.compute: Median milliseconds between consecutive SUBMIT events.
metrics.rationale: Spaced turns read as slow and composed.

metrics.name: Turn frequency
metrics.compute: SUBMIT count divided by elapsed session minutes.
metrics.rationale: More exchanges per minute is a faster, livelier rhythm.

metrics.name: Idle time after answer
metrics.compute: Seconds of no typing after RESPONSE_END before the next input event.
metrics.rationale: Silence after the answer points to disengagement or rest.

metrics.name: Window blur rate
metrics.compute: Window blur events per turn.
metrics.rationale: Leaving the window is a direct signal of divided attention.

metrics.name: Hidden-document time ratio
metrics.compute: Accumulated document hidden time divided by turn duration.
metrics.rationale: Time spent on another tab drains focus and drive.

metrics.name: Mouse activity rate
metrics.compute: Throttled pointermove plus click events per 10 s of session.
metrics.rationale: Restless pointer motion reads as activation, not necessarily focus.

metrics.name: Pointer near the eyes
metrics.compute: Share of pointer samples within 200 px of the presence/eyes element center.
metrics.rationale: Hovering near the face reads as engaging with the agent itself.

metrics.name: Duplicate resubmission rate
metrics.compute: Share of SUBMIT prompts with normalized similarity above 0.9 to the previous prompt.
metrics.rationale: Repeating the same prompt signals a stuck, unsure loop.

metrics.name: Keystroke cadence variance
metrics.compute: Coefficient of variation of inter-key intervals within a prompt.
metrics.rationale: An irregular typing rhythm reads as unsettled.

metrics.name: Question rate
metrics.compute: Share of the last 10 prompts containing a question mark, EMA-weighted.
metrics.rationale: Asking keeps the exchange open and directed at the agent.

metrics.name: Lexical entrainment with agent answer
metrics.compute: Jaccard overlap of content words (stopwords removed) between a prompt and the preceding agent answer.
metrics.rationale: Borrowing the agent's words is linguistic alignment, a closeness cue.

metrics.name: Topic shift score
metrics.compute: One minus the Jaccard overlap of content words between the current and previous prompt.
metrics.rationale: Jumping topics widens exploration but scatters attention.

metrics.name: Self-repetition rate
metrics.compute: Repeated 3-grams across the last 5 prompts divided by all 3-grams.
metrics.rationale: Repeating phrasing suggests a stalled, less certain user.

metrics.name: Confirmation rate
metrics.compute: Share of prompts of at most 3 words matching yes, ok, yeah, right, sure, got it.
metrics.rationale: Short affirmations signal agreement and a settled decision.

metrics.name: Backchannel rate
metrics.compute: Share of prompts matching hm, mm, ah, i see, ok then.
metrics.rationale: Backchannels are rapport signals that keep the partner talking.

metrics.name: Abort-signal rate
metrics.compute: Share of prompts containing stop, wait, never mind, forget it, cancel.
metrics.rationale: Abort language marks tension and lost confidence.

metrics.name: Politeness markers
metrics.compute: Occurrences of please, thanks, thank you, sorry, excuse me per 100 words.
metrics.rationale: Politeness raises formality and signals goodwill.

metrics.name: Formality score
metrics.compute: Average of binary cues: no contractions, capital I, terminal punctuation, no all-lowercase.
metrics.rationale: Careful orthography reads as formal and slightly distant.

metrics.name: Exclamation rate
metrics.compute: Exclamation marks per 100 words over the last 10 prompts.
metrics.rationale: Exclamations raise perceived activation and lightness.

metrics.name: Emoji rate
metrics.compute: Emoji code points per 100 characters, matched by Unicode ranges.
metrics.rationale: Emoji are a reliable marker of playfulness in chat.

metrics.name: Self-disclosure rate
metrics.compute: First-person singular pronouns plus feeling verbs per 100 words.
metrics.rationale: Talking about oneself deepens closeness and personal depth.

metrics.name: Hedging rate
metrics.compute: Occurrences of maybe, perhaps, i guess, kind of, sort of, not sure per 100 words.
metrics.rationale: Hedges mark uncertainty and mild unease.

metrics.name: Imperative rate
metrics.compute: Share of prompts whose first word is a bare verb (show, give, make, tell, explain, list), POS-checked.
metrics.rationale: Bare commands are assertive and direct, hence less formal.

metrics.name: Average sentence length
metrics.compute: Mean words per sentence over the last 5 prompts, sentence split on terminal punctuation.
metrics.rationale: Longer sentences pack more information and structure.

metrics.name: Vocabulary richness (Guiraud index)
metrics.compute: Unique lemmas divided by square root of token count over the last 5 prompts.
metrics.rationale: A wider vocabulary reads as deeper and more exploratory.
